applies_why: The judge text addresses a challenger's multi-verse covenant-origin analogy and then resolves it by pointing to Matthew 1:20's own wording.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires
room: never verse by verse: (1) a footed chain may not be answered by one verse's own wording; (2) a target verse's own wording may still be noted alongside the chain.
why: After acknowledging the challenger's chain is footed, the judge relies on the single sentence's own words rather than weighing the competing chains by footing, which is the verse-by-verse move K-C forbids.
